why_static_tifs_cannot_be_rescored_on_ca.theorem: Any final GeoTIFF emitted after masking or collar-pruning against full `existing_faults.tif` (or computing fault-tip/continuation rays from full `existing_faults.tif`) already conditions on all four holdout quadrants. Evaluating static full-catalogue `.tif` files against withheld `existing_faults.tif` folds introduces severe target leakage — biasing full-catalogue `d > 2 px` pruned maps downward (self-deleting near hidden faults, e.g. H33 drops from 0.0961 fold-fair to 0.0037 static) while biasing `2 < d <= 3 px` continuation halos artificially upward. Only fold-strict OOF holdout evaluations computed from `visible_fold` alone are valid `HOLDOUT-DTI` measurements.

sparse_binary_dot_field_pigeonhole_proof.statement: Even if all continuous probability surfaces are discarded or top-k thresholded, sparse binary dot raster `13GEMSDOE:docs/downloads/13gems_20261001_r13-lattice-s5_v2_zerofill.tif` (SHA-256 `c12533bb980234c3a706af641d4f1d514bbbe482714b2ebcac3b10f3e72a7a3f`, `206,895` binary dots) covers `5,099,871` / `5,106,385` allowed cells (`99.872434%`), leaving only `6,514` allowed cells uncovered across the entire GeoDAWN grid. By the Pigeonhole Principle, EVERY possible binary map with `k >= 21,714` dots has forward 3-px overlap > 0.70 against this binary raster, and EVERY possible 37,654-dot map has forward 3-px overlap >= 0.827004 > 0.70.
